mainTopic: מעילה through an agent: who is liable (בעל הבית, שליח, or חנווני), and how much must go against the instructions
overview: First the גמרא finishes an earlier point. A שליח who adds to his errand does not cancel the בעל הבית's liability for מעילה. Then a new משנה rules that if the שליח follows the spoken instructions, the בעל הבית is liable, even if he claims he privately meant something else. If the שליח changes the instructions, the שליח is liable. When a חרש שוטה וקטן carries the money, the בעל הבית is liable if they do the errand, and the חנווני is liable if they do not. If the owner remembers that the money is הקדש in time, he can redeem it onto another פרוטה or a utensil. The גמרא explains that דברים שבלב אינם דברים. It gives two answers for how a חרש שוטה וקטן can carry out an errand: רבי אלעזר's vat of olives and רבי יוחנן's עירוב on an animal. רב ששת then settles a contradiction from a ברייתא: the חנווני is liable only when both the owner and the שליח remembered. A second משנה teaches that half a פרוטה is not enough for מעילה, but two full פרוטות can make both people liable, with רבי יהודה disagreeing about the owner. A new case about a gold dinar begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the משנה had to teach that the homeowner is still liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the earlier ruling was needed. Without it, we might think the שליח's extra action cancels the בעל הבית's agency, so the בעל הבית would not be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that the agent uprooted the homeowner's agency, so the homeowner would not be liable for מעילה. The משנה teaches us that he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the earlier ruling in the משנה was needed. It closes the previous discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case before this was a שליח who did what he was sent to do and also added more on his own. One could think that by adding, the שליח broke away from the בעל הבית's mission altogether. The משנה tells us no: the part done as instructed still counts as the בעל הבית's act, so he is liable for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / you might have thought
He uprooted (cancelled) his agency
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)
To be liable for מעילה (misuse of הקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: Even if a שליח adds to his errand, the part he did as instructed is still the בעל הבית's act.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
the agent uprooted the agency of the homeowner,
and so the homeowner should not be liable for misuse —
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's explanation from the previous section of why the משנה's ruling was necessary.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שליח's additions do not cancel the agency, so the בעל הבית remains liable for the part done as instructed.

steps.title: Agent followed instructions, owner claims he meant something else
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: the בעל הבית told the שליח to bring from a specific place, and the שליח did. The בעל הבית says he really meant the other place. The בעל הבית is still liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he told him, 'Bring me from the window' or 'from the chest,' and he brought it from there, then even if the homeowner says, 'In my heart I only meant the other place,' the homeowner is liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The first case: the שליח did exactly what he was told, so the בעל הבית is liable, whatever he says he was thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agency depends on the words the בעל הבית actually said, not on private thoughts he never expressed. Since the שליח followed the spoken instructions, the act counts as the בעל הבית's, and he is liable for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Window (a niche in the wall where things were kept)
A chest or box
It was not in my heart (I did not really mean it)
He is liable for מעילה

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'or' does not mean the owner gave two choices. It means 'either example': he named one place, the window or the chest, and the agent brought from that place.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he said to him:
"Bring me something from the window"
or "from the chest," and he brought it to him from there.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת:
phrases.english: Even though the homeowner says:
"In my heart I meant only that other place,"
and he brought it from this place —
the homeowner is liable for misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר לוֹ: הָבֵא לִי מִן הַחַלּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new set of agency cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שליח follows the spoken instructions, the בעל הבית is liable for מעילה, even if he claims he privately meant otherwise.

steps.title: Agent switched locations, so the agent is liable
steps.stepSummary: If the שליח was told one place and brought from the other, the שליח, not the בעל הבית, is liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he told him, 'Bring me from the window,' and he brought from the chest, or 'from the chest,' and he brought from the window, the agent is liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. The שליח did not do what he was told, so the liability moves to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the שליח changes the instructions, he is no longer carrying out the בעל הבית's errand. The act becomes his own, so he is the one who did מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent, messenger
Agency, the errand given to an agent

steps.whatToRemember: Followed instructions → בעל הבית liable. Changed instructions → שליח liable.

phrases.english: But if he said to him:
"Bring me something from the window,"
and he brought it to him from the chest,
or he said "from the chest,"
and he brought it to him from the window —
the agent is liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 2: here the שליח changed the instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who goes against the instructions is himself liable for מעילה.

steps.title: Sending through a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor
steps.stepSummary: If a חרש שוטה וקטן carries the money and does what they were told, the בעל הבית is liable. If they do something else, the חנווני is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sent the money through a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor: if they did his errand, the homeowner is liable for מעילה; if they did not do his errand, the storekeeper is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a case where the messenger is a חרש שוטה וקטן, people who cannot normally be legal agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though they are not real שלוחים, when they carry out the errand exactly, the result is what the בעל הבית wanted, so he is liable. If they go off on their own, nothing can be pinned on the בעל הבית, and the חנווני who received the money is the one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor: people without full legal responsibility
Storekeeper
They carried out his errand

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that a חרש שוטה וקטן counts as a real שליח. The משנה only looks at whether the owner's wish was actually carried out.

phrases.english: If he sent it by the hand of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor,
if they carried out his errand —
the homeowner is liable for misuse;
if they did not carry out his errand —
the storekeeper is liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the agency cases to messengers who cannot legally be שלוחים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a חרש שוטה וקטן: errand done → בעל הבית liable; errand not done → חנווני liable.

steps.title: Owner remembers it is consecrated before the agent reaches the store
steps.stepSummary: If the בעל הבית sent a פקח and remembered the money was הקדש before the שליח reached the store, the חנווני is liable once he spends the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sent it through a competent person and remembered before the agent reached the storekeeper, the storekeeper is liable for מעילה when he spends the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the בעל הבית's mistake ends partway through the errand, so the liability moves to the חנווני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה applies to someone who uses הקדש by mistake. Once the בעל הבית remembers, he is no longer making a mistake, so he is not liable. The חנווני, who still does not know, becomes liable at the moment he spends the money.

keyTerms.meaning: A competent, legally responsible person
And he remembered
When he spends it

steps.whatToRemember: מעילה is tied to acting by mistake. When the owner remembers in time, he is no longer liable. Step 15 shows that the חנווני is liable only if the שליח also remembered; otherwise the שליח is liable.

phrases.english: If he sent it by the hand of a competent person,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִזְכַּר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ אֵצֶל חֶנְווֹנִי –
phrases.english: and he remembered before the agent reached the storekeeper —
phrases.notes: He remembered that the money was הקדש.

phrases.english: the storekeeper is liable for misuse when he spends it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 4: now the messenger is a פקח, and the twist is that the owner remembers in the middle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the בעל הבית remembers before the שליח reaches the store, the חנווני is liable once he spends the money.

steps.title: The fix: redeem the הקדש money onto something else
steps.stepSummary: The בעל הבית can save the חנווני from מעילה by redeeming the הקדש פרוטה onto another פרוטה or a utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should he do? He takes a פרוטה or a utensil and says: 'The הקדש פרוטה, wherever it is, is redeemed onto this.' This works because הקדש can be redeemed with money or with something worth money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the case from Step 5 by telling the בעל הבית how to keep the חנווני from being liable for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the חנווני would be liable once he spends the money. Here the בעל הבית moves the קדושה off the coins onto his own פרוטה or utensil. The coins in the store become regular money, so nobody commits מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin that counts as money in הלכה
Property that belongs to the Temple
Redeemed; its holiness has moved off it
Is redeemed
Something worth money, such as a utensil

steps.whatToRemember: הקדש can be redeemed even when it is not in front of you, and you can redeem it with money or with any item worth money.

phrases.english: What should he do?
phrases.notes: "He" is the בעל הבית from Step 5, who remembered that the money was הקדש.

phrases.english: He takes a perutah or a utensil,
and says: "The perutah of hekdesh,
wherever it is,
is redeemed onto this,"
for hekdesh is redeemed
with money and with something worth money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the solution for the case in Step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בעל הבית redeems the הקדש פרוטה onto another פרוטה or a utensil, so the חנווני spends regular money and nobody commits מעילה.

steps.title: What is the משנה teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new idea is taught by the case where the בעל הבית claims he meant a different place.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what lesson we learn from the משנה case in Step 2. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in Step 2 seems obvious, since the שליח did exactly what he was told. So the גמרא wants to know what the point of that case is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What is it teaching us? This asks for the new idea a ruling teaches.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the case in Step 2, where the בעל הבית said, "I really meant the other place."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא and goes back to the earlier משנה case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new lesson the Step 2 case teaches

steps.title: Thoughts in the heart do not count
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is that unspoken intentions have no legal power.
steps.simpleTranslation: Things in the heart are not things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה teaches us that a person's private, unspoken thoughts do not count in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל הבית said one place out loud but claims he meant the other. Since only his spoken words count, the שליח did his job, and the בעל הבית is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Thoughts kept in the heart have no legal effect

steps.whatToRemember: What you say counts. What you only think does not.

phrases.english: Things that are in the heart
are not things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה teaches that דברים שבלב אינם דברים, so the בעל הבית is liable.

steps.title: How can a חרש, שוטה, or קטן be a שליח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a חרש שוטה וקטן and asks how they can act for the בעל הבית when they cannot be agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent the money with a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן: if they did what he said, and so on. But they cannot be agents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה from Step 4 and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש שוטה וקטן do not have the legal standing to be a שליח. So how can their action make the בעל הבית liable, as if they were his agents?

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who in הלכה lacks legal competence
A mentally incompetent person
A minor
People who can legally serve as agents

phrases.english: He sent it in the hand of a deaf-mute,
an imbecile, or a minor,
if they did what he said, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points back to the rest of the משנה: then the בעל הבית is liable.

phrases.english: But they are not able to be agents!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (Step 4) that the בעל הבית is liable when a חרש שוטה וקטן do what he said
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being liable through someone else requires a valid agent, and these people cannot be agents.

steps.title: They are like a vat of olives
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the חכמים treated them like a vat of olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: They treated them like a vat of olives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר begins answering the challenge by comparing these people to a vat of olives. The explanation of this comparison comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid that leaks from olives in a vat counts as if the owner wanted it there, because he is happy it is there. In the same way, the חכמים treat the actions of a חרש שוטה וקטן as done with the בעל הבית's intent, since he is pleased they did what he asked. They are not real agents, but their action is linked to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A vat where olives are piled up so their liquid seeps out
They (the חכמים) treated them as

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying a חרש שוטה וקטן become real שלוחים. He is saying that their action counts as done with the בעל הבית's intent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
They treated them like a vat of olives,
phrases.notes: In the olive case, the owner counts as wanting the liquid that leaks out, even though he did nothing himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עֲשָׂאוּם כְּמַעֲטָן שֶׁל זֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a known case in another area of הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since they cannot be agents, their actions should not be linked to the בעל הבית at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like liquid in an olive vat, their action counts as done with the בעל הבית's intent because he is pleased with it, so he is liable.

steps.title: The source for the vat of olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in טהרות. It says olives can become טמא only from the moisture in the vat, not the moisture in the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: from when can olives become טמא? From when they give off the moisture of the vat, but not the moisture of the basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing where רבי אלעזר's comparison to a 'vat of olives' comes from. It quotes the משנה about when olives become able to get טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moisture in the vat helps make oil, so the owner wants it there. That is why it counts, even though no person poured it. Moisture in the basket just drips away and does nothing, so it does not count. In the same way, when a חרש, שוטה וקטן does what the owner wanted, the owner's wish is what makes it count.

keyTerms.meaning: A vat where olives are stored so they soften before pressing
A basket; liquid drips out through its holes
Moisture or 'sweat' that comes out of the olives
Become able to become ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: Food can only become טמא after a liquid the owner wants has touched it. That is why the vat moisture counts and the basket moisture does not.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: olives,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in טהרות 9:1. It is the 'vat of olives' רבי אלעזר just mentioned.

phrases.english: from when do they become able to get טומאה?
From when they give off the moisture of the vat,
but not the moisture of the basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source text behind רבי אלעזר's comparison in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that what a חרש, שוטה וקטן does can count because it carries out the owner's wish
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in טהרות 9:1 about vat moisture and basket moisture

steps.title: A monkey or elephant carrying an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives another answer. It is like an עירוב sent on a monkey or an elephant: the job still gets done, so here too the job gets done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is like what we learned. If someone put an עירוב on a monkey or an elephant and it carried it there, and he told another person to take it from the animal, it is a valid עירוב. So we see the task gets carried out. Here too, the task gets carried out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from step 9 in a different way. He compares the case to an עירוב carried by an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A monkey or elephant can never be a שליח, yet the עירוב still works once a real person takes it at the other end. So the job can be completed even without a proper שליח. The same is true when a חרש, שוטה וקטן brings the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Food placed to extend the area a person may walk on שבת
The job a messenger is sent to do
Monkey
Elephant
'Evidently'; we can see from here

steps.whyThisMatters: There are now two answers to the same question: רבי אלעזר's vat of olives and רבי יוחנן's עירוב on an animal.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: it is like that which we learned:
if he put it on a monkey and it carried it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the food for the עירוב.

phrases.english: or on an elephant and it carried it,
and he told another person to take it from the animal,
it is a valid עירוב.
Evidently, it does carry out his errand.
Here too, his errand has been carried out.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, where a חרש, שוטה וקטן brought the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the קשיא of step 9, alongside רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (an עירוב sent by an animal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חרש, שוטה וקטן cannot be a שליח, so nothing they do on the owner's behalf should count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without a valid שליח, the errand can be completed, as with an עירוב carried by an animal and taken by a person.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a competent messenger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of sending the money with a פקח. It points out that the חנווני is liable even though the messenger did not remember.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he sent it with a competent person, and so on. This means the חנווני is liable even though the messenger did not remember.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next case in the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only the owner remembering, and still makes the חנווני liable. From this the גמרא infers that the messenger's memory does not matter. That inference is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A competent adult who can serve as a שליח
Messenger or agent
Remembered (here, that the money was הקדש)

phrases.english: 'If he sent it with a competent person,' and so on.
phrases.notes: Our משנה continues: if the owner remembered before it reached the store, the חנווני is liable.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִידְּכַר שָׁלִיחַ.
phrases.english: And this is so even though the messenger did not remember.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the חרש, שוטה וקטן discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the plain reading of the משנה, if the owner remembers, the חנווני is liable even if the messenger did not remember.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the messenger is liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if only the owner remembered, the messenger is liable, not the חנווני. This contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a contradiction is raised: if the owner remembered and the messenger did not, the messenger is liable. If both remembered, the חנווני is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the inference from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to say the חנווני is liable when only the owner remembered. The ברייתא says that in that case the messenger is the one who did מעילה. In the ברייתא, the חנווני is liable only when both remembered.

keyTerms.meaning: Committed מעילה, misuse of הקדש property
Storekeeper
The owner who sent the money

phrases.english: And a contradiction is raised: if the owner remembered
and the messenger did not remember, the messenger is liable for מעילה;
if both remembered, the storekeeper is liable for מעילה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי: נִזְכַּר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת וְלֹא נִזְכַּר שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the חנווני is liable even when only the owner remembered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that when only the owner remembered, the messenger is liable. The חנווני is liable only when both remembered.

steps.title: The משנה means both remembered
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the משנה is also talking about a case where both the owner and the messenger remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: our משנה too is talking about a case where both of them remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת settles the contradiction by explaining the משנה more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference that the messenger did not remember was wrong. The משנה is talking about a case where both remembered, just like the ברייתא. So both sources agree: the חנווני is liable only when both the owner and the messenger remembered.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: When a competent messenger is sent, the חנווני is liable only if both the owner and the messenger remembered. If only the owner remembered, the messenger is liable.

phrases.english: רב ששת said: our משנה too is talking
about a case where both of them remembered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי, כְּשֶׁנִּזְכְּרוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה makes the חנווני liable even when the messenger did not remember.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a case where both remembered, so it agrees with the ברייתא.

steps.title: Half lamps, half wicks: neither one is liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the owner asked for half lamps and half wicks and the שליח spent the whole פרוטה on one item, or the reverse, neither the owner nor the שליח is liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He gave him a פרוטה and said, 'Bring me lamps with half and wicks with half,' and the messenger brought all wicks or all lamps. Or the owner said, 'Bring me all lamps' or 'all wicks,' and the messenger brought half lamps and half wicks. Neither of them committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives cases where the שליח only partly followed the owner's instructions, and it rules that nobody is liable for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, only half the פרוטה was spent the way the owner said, and the other half was spent the שליח's own way. Half a פרוטה is less than the minimum amount for מעילה. So the owner is not liable for his half, and the שליח is not liable for his half.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
The smallest coin. It is the minimum amount for מעילה.
Lamps.
Wicks.
They did not commit מְעִילָה, misuse of הקדש property.

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases look like opposites, but they share the same logic. In both, exactly half a פרוטה matches the owner's words and half does not. Neither half reaches the minimum of a full פרוטה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
He gave him a peruta, and said to him:
"Bring me lamps with half of it
and wicks with half of it"
and he went and brought him wicks with all of it
or lamps with all of it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: ״הָבֵא לִי בְּכוּלָּהּ נֵרוֹת״,
phrases.english: or where he said to him: "Bring me lamps with all of it,"
or "wicks with all of it,"
and he went and brought lamps with half of it
and wicks with half of it —
neither of them is liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished discussing the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only half a פרוטה follows the owner's instructions and half does not, neither the owner nor the שליח is liable for מעילה.

steps.title: Swapping the stores makes the messenger liable
steps.stepSummary: If the owner named a specific store for the lamps and a specific store for the wicks, and the שליח swapped the stores, the שליח is liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said, 'Bring me lamps with half from this place and wicks with half from that place,' and the messenger brought lamps from the wicks' place and wicks from the lamps' place, the שליח committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a contrasting case. Here the שליח is liable because he went against the instructions with the entire פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, half the money still followed the instructions. Here both halves went wrong, because each item came from the wrong place. So the שליח departed from the instructions with a full פרוטה, and he is the one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Such-and-such place, meaning a specific store.
The messenger or agent.
He committed מְעִילָה and is liable.

phrases.english: But if he said to him:
"Bring me lamps with half of it from such-and-such place
and wicks with half of it from such-and-such place,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהָלַךְ וְהֵבִיא לוֹ נֵרוֹת מִמְּקוֹם פְּתִילוֹת,
phrases.english: and he went and brought him lamps from the place meant for wicks,
and wicks from the place meant for lamps —
the messenger is liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 16. Here the whole פרוטה goes against the instructions, not just half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שליח goes against the instructions with a full פרוטה, even when that is made up of two halves, the שליח is liable for מעילה.

steps.title: One אתרוג and one pomegranate: both are liable
steps.stepSummary: The owner gave two פרוטות for an אתרוג. The שליח bought an אתרוג with one and a pomegranate with the other. The תנא קמא rules that both the owner and the שליח are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave him two פרוטות and said, 'Go bring me an אתרוג.' He brought an אתרוג with one and a pomegranate with the other. Both of them committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case with two full פרוטות, where one was spent as instructed and one was not. It rules that both people are liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אתרוג bought with one פרוטה fulfills the owner's request, so the owner is liable for that פרוטה. The pomegranate bought with the other פרוטה goes against the instructions, so the שליח is liable for that one. Unlike the half-פרוטה cases, each side here reaches a full פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two פרוטות, enough for two separate full units of מעילה.
A citron.
A pomegranate.
Both of them are liable for מעילה.

phrases.english: He gave him two perutot,
and said to him: "Go and bring me an etrog,"
and he went and brought him an etrog with one
and a pomegranate with one —
both of them are liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from half-פרוטה cases to a case with two full פרוטות, where each person's share reaches the minimum.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one full פרוטה follows the instructions and one goes against them, the owner and the שליח are each liable.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the owner is not liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. The בעל הבית is not liable, because he can claim he wanted one big אתרוג worth both פרוטות, not a small, poor one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The homeowner did not commit מעילה, because he can say to him, 'I wanted a big אתרוג, and you brought me a small, poor one.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the previous ruling. He says only the שליח is liable, and the owner is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sees the small אתרוג as fulfilling the owner's request. רבי יהודה says the owner meant to spend both פרוטות on one big אתרוג. So a one-פרוטה אתרוג is not what he asked for, his instructions were not carried out at all, and he is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The homeowner, who sent the שליח.
A big אתרוג, worth both פרוטות.
Small and poor quality.

steps.whatToRemember: Basic rule of this משנה: whoever's instructions are actually carried out with a full פרוטה is liable. The owner is liable if his request was done, and the שליח is liable if he went against it. רבי יהודה adds that a cheaper version of what the owner asked for may not count as doing his request.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The homeowner is not liable for misuse,
because he can say to him:
"I was looking for a big etrog,
and you brought me a small, poor one."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לֹא מָעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion on the אתרוג case in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, only the שליח is liable, because a one-פרוטה אתרוג does not fulfill a request for an אתרוג bought with two פרוטות.

steps.title: New case: a gold dinar sent for a robe
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: the owner gave the שליח a gold dinar of הקדש and told him to buy a robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave him a gold dinar and said to him: Go and bring me a robe,
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The משנה describes the start of a new case, and the ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the cases used small coins. Now the owner gives a large coin, a דינר זהב. The setup prepares a case about how the שליח spends a bigger sum, and the ruling is not given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A gold dinar, a high-value coin.
A robe or shirt.

phrases.english: He gave him a gold dinar,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: לֵךְ וְהָבֵא לִי חָלוּק,
phrases.english: and said to him: Go and bring me a robe,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next case in the same משנה, this time with a large coin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: the owner sends a gold dinar of הקדש to buy a robe. The ruling follows on the next amud.
